content: 1. Current hepatitis C infection in liver transplant recipients who are anti-HBc-positive has been discussed in the context of transplantation outcomes. 2. Tuberculosis and HIV co-infection in individuals who inject drugs necessitates integrated services for tuberculosis, HIV, prison health, and harm reduction. 3. Managing tuberculosis in individuals who use and inject illicit drugs requires tailored approaches to address the unique challenges in this population. 4. A high prevalence of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection has been observed among tuberculosis patients, both with and without HIV, in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. 5. Vietnamese immigrants to the United States show significant prevalence and interaction of hepatitis B and latent tuberculosis infections. 6. Co-infection with hepatitis B or C in individuals with HIV can impact liver function, particularly when anti-tuberculosis drugs are administered. 7. The interplay between metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease and viral hepatitis significantly influences liver disease severity, as shown in a large community-based study in a viral endemic area. 8. Fatty liver is associated with significant liver inflammation and exacerbates advanced fibrosis in patients with chronic HBV infection. 9. Chronic hepatitis B infection in children with nonalcoholic fatty liver disease is linked to hepatic steatosis and liver injury. 10. Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is associated with less severe liver fibrosis in patients with chronic hepatitis B, as demonstrated in a multi-center retrospective study. 11. The incidence and risk factors for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) development have been reviewed, highlighting key contributors to disease progression. 12. Tenofovir alafenamide therapy in chronic HBV patients significantly increases serum lipid levels compared to entecavir therapy. 13. Managing cirrhosis in resource-limited settings, such as sub-Saharan Africa, presents unique challenges and requires innovative approaches. 14. The risk of hepatocellular carcinoma decreases in HBV-related cirrhotic patients who achieve recompensation, based on Baveno VII criteria. 15. Hepatitis B virus-related cryoglobulinemic vasculitis presents with specific clinical manifestations, and antiviral therapy plays a critical role in management. 16. Chronic HBV infection can lead to extrahepatic manifestations, and antiviral therapy is essential in mitigating these effects. 17. Hepatitis B infection can involve renal complications, with a spectrum of presentations ranging from mild to severe. 18. Renal impairment in chronic hepatitis B patients has been reviewed, emphasizing the need for careful monitoring and management. 19. Demyelinating polyneuropathy has been associated with chronic inactive hepatitis B infection, highlighting a rare but significant neurological complication. 20. Plasma exchange-based non-bioartificial liver support systems improve short-term outcomes in patients with HBV-associated acute-on-chronic liver failure. 21. Sequential use of high-volume plasma exchange and continuous renal replacement therapy has been reported in managing HBV-related acute liver failure. 22. Hepatic decompensation after nucleos(t)ide analog withdrawal has been studied in a large, international, multiethnic cohort of chronic HBV patients. 23. Serious adverse events following cessation of nucleos(t)ide analogs in chronic HBV patients have been systematically reviewed and analyzed. 24. Safety considerations for withdrawing nucleos(t)ide analogs in chronic HBV patients emphasize the principle of first, do no harm. 25. HBV reactivation associated with new classes of immunosuppressants and immunomodulators has been systematically reviewed, with expert opinions provided. 26. HBV-associated acute liver failure following immunosuppression carries a significant risk of mortality, necessitating prompt and effective management. 27. The natural history of acute hepatitis B surface antigen-positive hepatitis in Greek adults has been documented, providing insights into disease progression. 28. Lamivudine has been shown to be safe and effective in patients with severe acute or fulminant hepatitis B, based on multicenter experiences. 29. Persistent HBV viremia with polymerase mutations has been observed among HIV/HBV co-infected patients on HBV-active antiretroviral therapy in South Africa. 30. Postpartum hepatitis flares in women with chronic HBV infection have been characterized, with predictors identified for better management. 31. Clinical and virological predictors of hepatic flares in pregnant women with chronic HBV infection have been studied, providing guidance for monitoring and intervention. 32. Strategies for preventing peripartum hepatitis B transmission have been outlined, emphasizing the importance of timely interventions. 33. Preventing transmission of bloodborne viruses from infected healthcare workers to patients has been addressed in a new Canadian guideline. 34. The clinical and occupational health management of healthcare workers living with chronic HBV has been reviewed, with comparisons to UK and international policies. 35. Chronic hepatitis B prevalence among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Australians has been systematically reviewed, particularly in the context of universal vaccination. 36. The prevalence of hepatitis B in India has been systematically reviewed and analyzed, providing a comprehensive understanding of the disease burden. 37. Chronic liver disease in Aboriginal North Americans has been reviewed, highlighting the unique challenges faced by this population. 38. Viral hepatitis in the Arctic has been studied, shedding light on the epidemiology and management of the disease in this region. 39. Hepatitis D virus infection has been reviewed, with a focus on its clinical implications and management strategies.
